chapter: The Washingtonians, Bechet and drum style
title: Staged fires at the Kentucky Club and the gold cymbal
summary: The boss arranged fires when business was slack; Greer polished smoked cymbals and sold one to a California Ramblers drummer.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: I had a cymbal -- They had a band called the California Ramblers, a big white band, and the drummer was Stanley somebody. They were a good band, they could play, big band, so we had a fire. That was the ritual--the fire, when a holiday come up like the -- what's that day -- Palm Sunday or something, the boss Leo Bernstein come up and say, "hey

you all take your horns home, we're going to have an accident down there tonight. Sonny, leave them drums just like they are." I'd take the cymbals and put them in the piano and pull the lid down, because cymbals ain't going to burn. Man, now remember this is on 49th and Broadway. Man, that morning we get off and go across the street, next to Jack Dempsey's hang out there and drink before we go to Harlem, I was standing up there drinking with some boys in our gang, and get to lollygagging, here come the fire engines, the hook and ladder, there my drum sitting up on the ladder. Sitting up on the hook and ladder.

I swear before God, I ain't exaggerating and lying, that was New York. See, business would get slack. What do you call that. Sort of a two-three week holiday, slow or something like that, we'd have a fire over there. Next day, the insurance people would be rebuilding the club and the boss would tell me, "Sonny, go get a new set of drums."

So I take the cymbal out there and it be all smoked up, and I get me a ten-cent can of brass polish and shine it, sparkle -- this guy with the California Rambler, he would come in there and say, 'hey, Sonny, how your cymbals?' I said, 'Man, that's a gold cymbal, what are you talking about.' Shine, you know. 'That's a gold cymbal.' He say, 'You want to sell it?' I'd say, 'oh, no man, I couldn't sell it. It's a gold cymbal. I won't sell it.' Say, 'sell it to me man, he'd give me 25 or 30
"Go on, you're my buddy, dollars, I'd say, go on and take it." I'd borrow one from the drum store and write to the factory, they'd send me a couple more. Cost nothing.
